provenance.note: Quotes checked against each source's text layer on 2026-10-20. PHED reports and the 2025-26 and 2026-27 budget speeches are Hindi in a legacy (Kruti Dev) font: the text-layer string is the check, and the Hindi was read from the page images. Four High Court orders and one judgment were read from LiveLaw and Verdictum copies that carry the court's own upload stamps.

headline: What has been promised about Jaipur's water, and by when
intro: Twenty-one commitments on Jaipur's water supply, new sources, sewers and drains, the Dravyavati river and Ramgarh dam, each on a dated document: PHED's annual progress reports, the State's budget speeches, MoHUA's AMRUT 2.0 progress report, a note of the National Water Development Agency, or a court order. Four are delivered: two later than the date PHED or JDA had set, one ahead of it, and one that never had a published date. Four are past their date with no completion on record, two of them after PHED had moved the date once. For thirteen the promise can be cited but its current status cannot yet be cited either way; most are budget announcements that gave no date.

status_legend.delivered: The promised thing verifiably happened, even if late. The dates show how late.
status_legend.on-track: The stated date has not passed and the latest dated evidence is consistent with it.
status_legend.slipped: The institution itself has moved the date. Old and new dates are both shown.
status_legend.overdue: The promised date has passed with no delivery and no formally revised date we can cite.
status_legend.stalled: Work or approvals have stopped, by the institution's own account or a court's.
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

update_model: Statuses change only against a dated citation. The register is re-checked each January against PHED's annual progress report, each February against the State budget and its announcement lists, monthly against MoHUA's AMRUT 2.0 progress report, and after hearings of the Rajasthan High Court on Ramgarh dam and the Dravyavati. A passed next-check date with no new citation is flagged, never silently updated.
sources_note: PHED's progress reports and the 2025-26 and 2026-27 budget speeches are printed in Hindi in a legacy font that does not extract as text; their figures were read from the page images. MoHUA's AMRUT 2.0 report still names the two former corporations (Jaipur Heritage and Jaipur Greater); rows keep those names as MoHUA prints them. Court orders were read from copies published by LiveLaw and Verdictum; the court, case number and date are the citation.

commitments.title: Bisalpur water for the area between Diggi-Malpura Road and Tonk Road (zones S-15 to S-18)
commitments.committed_by: Public Health Engineering Department (PHED), Rajasthan
commitments.what: To bring Bisalpur water to the area between Diggi-Malpura Road and Tonk Road, including the Sitapura industrial area, PHED sanctioned Rs 114.73 crore on 6 May 2021: 8 elevated reservoirs and a 358 km distribution network. In January 2025 PHED put the work at 95% with the rest due by February 2025. Its two reports give different work-order dates (6 October 2022 and 18 April 2022).

commitments.title: Ramgarh dam: clearing its catchment so water reaches the lake again
commitments.committed_by: Government of Rajasthan, under directions of the Rajasthan High Court in Suo Motu v State of Rajasthan (D.B. Civil Writ Petition 11153/2011, first heard as S.B. Civil Writ Petition 11153/2011)
commitments.what: Ramgarh dam (completed in 1901 by CWC's dam register, 1903 by the Supreme Court's judgment) supplied irrigation until 1978 and then Jaipur's drinking water, and has been dry for years. On 23 August 2011 the High Court directed that the State 'will ensure stoppage of encroachment and construction in the catchment area of Ramgarh Dam' and 'will come out with the plan for removal of encroachments so as to restore the position as was existing on 15.08.1947'. The State prepared an initial action plan in July 2012 and a technical committee reported on 9 January 2013. No date for restoring inflow has been set.

commitment_source.label: Supreme Court, SLP (C) 38040-38041 of 2012, NIMS University v State of Rajasthan, judgment of 9 November 2017, paras 7-8 and 12

status_history.note: The High Court set up a two-member monitoring committee and issued directions on encroachment in the four tehsils of the catchment; a final order followed on 29 May 2012.
status_history.source_label: Supreme Court, SLP (C) 38040-38041 of 2012, NIMS University v State of Rajasthan, judgment of 9 November 2017, paras 7-10

status_history.note: The Supreme Court recorded that it had asked whether there was any water in Ramgarh Lake 'but were told that it is still bone dry', and that little had changed on the ground since the High Court's orders; it ordered one construction in the catchment demolished by 30 November 2017.
status_history.source_label: Supreme Court, SLP (C) 38040-38041 of 2012, NIMS University v State of Rajasthan, judgment of 9 November 2017, paras 13, 37 and 42

status_history.note: The High Court asked for a full affidavit, through the Advocate General with the Jaipur Collector, on encroachments and buildings in the catchment in Andhi, Jamwa Ramgarh, Amer, Shahpura and Viratnagar tehsils and on steps taken since 2013, and directed the Water Resources Department to remove anicuts that block flow towards the lake.
status_history.source_label: Rajasthan High Court (Jaipur), D.B. Civil Writ Petition 11153/2011 (Suo Motu), order of 30 July 2026 (LiveLaw copy)

status_history.note: The Collector's affidavit listed the encroachers. The Advocate General said a removal drive is continuing; the court directed the list be published in Rajasthan Patrika and Dainik Bhaskar as 15 days' notice, after which the State is to remove the encroachments. Next hearing 15 September 2026; that order has not been read.
status_history.source_label: Rajasthan High Court (Jaipur), D.B. Civil Writ Petition 11153/2011 (Suo Motu), order of 13 August 2026 (LiveLaw copy)
